properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony's idea, 2026-08-31, thinking out loud about a systematic cleanup sweep. Nothing here is intent and nothing has been chosen.

THE QUESTION. He wants dead code eliminated. Before scheduling that, what would actually SHOW it? Two instruments were checked and neither answers today:

· THE COMPILER CANNOT SEE IT. `reflow2-core` is a library crate, so every `pub` item is public API and Rust's `dead_code` lint never fires on it. A clean build is therefore NOT evidence of no dead code — it is the instrument being blind. Same shape as the 40x method artefact measured this morning: the obvious measurement returns "nothing here" and reads as an all-clear.

· THE DESIGN'S OWN TOOL REFUSES, ON PURPOSE. `consumption_report` exists for exactly this question and answers: a consumer is recorded for 20 of 181 built capabilities (11%), below the 50% at which absence carries signal, so the 161 unconsumed are WITHHELD and the ratio is the finding. That refusal is correct — at 11% the list would report the modelling style, not what is unused.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
① MODEL CONSUMPTION UP PAST 50%, so the tool starts answering. Expensive in edges, and it makes reflow2 able to answer the question for USERS too, not just here.
② A CODE-LEVEL SWEEP that needs no design: `unreachable_pub`, or downgrading `pub` to `pub(crate)` and seeing what fails to compile. Cheap, mechanical, and blind to anything reachable-but-never-called.
③ COVERAGE-BASED — run the suite and the real binary, see what never executes. Catches what ② cannot; needs a harness and conflates "untested" with "unused".
④ ACCEPT THAT WE CANNOT CHEAPLY KNOW, and do not run the sweep. A legitimate answer the optimize skill explicitly permits ("allows the answer 'nothing here'").

⚠️ COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside rather than used to argue him down: there is currently NO MEASUREMENT that meaningful dead code exists here at all. The premise of the sweep is unmeasured, and ①–③ are all ways of testing the premise rather than ways of doing the work.
properties.name: OPEN — what instrument can actually see dead or unused code in reflow2, given the compiler is blind to it and the design's own tool refuses to answer?
properties.rationale:
Recorded under the brainstorm discipline: the ideas enter the graph labelled as ideas so nothing is lost and nothing is claimed as intent. Anthony has not chosen any option and none should be read as recommended by its position.

📌 WHY THIS IS SEPARATE FROM THE TWO NODES IT WAS OFFERED AGAINST, having read them: `req:the-design-says-what-was-built-and-never-used` is accepted INTENT that the design surface such things, and `cap:built-and-consumed-by-nothing` is the BUILT capability that does it. Both exist and work. This question is about what to do given that the built capability, correctly, declines to answer at 11% modelled consumption — an instrument question, not a request for the capability.
